questions.stem: What happens if blood glucose levels exceed the renal threshold?

options.text: The kidneys stop filtering blood to protect the nephrons
All the excess glucose is converted to glycogen in the kidney
Glucose appears in the urine because the PCT cannot reabsorb it all
The collecting duct absorbs the extra glucose instead

questions.explanation: When blood glucose is very high (above the renal threshold), there is too much glucose for the transport proteins in the PCT to reabsorb. The excess glucose remains in the filtrate and appears in the urine, which is a sign of diabetes.
